name: Melvins
label: AmRep
lede: Three Montesano high schoolers who named themselves after a Thriftway supervisor, taught Kurt Cobain what punk was, then kept going for four decades through a major label, a mirror-image record and two drum kits bolted together.

eras.title: Three kids from Montesano
eras.text: A logging-town high school band that started on Hendrix and The Who covers and swerved into hardcore, then slowed everything down. By the end of it Dale Crover was behind the kit, Kurt Cobain was hanging around the practice space, and the first records were out.

years.cap: Montesano, Washington. Osborne, Lukin and Dillard were high school classmates.
years.src: Wikipedia: Melvins · Consequence: Three Bastards, 30 Years
years.h: Montesano: [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]], [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] and [[Mike Dillard|a3750a7b-cf02-4e48-b16c-0b61ca820bfa]] start a band
years.p: Three high school classmates play Jimi Hendrix and The Who covers before turning to hardcore punk. The name comes from a supervisor at a local Thriftway store, chosen because it sounded appropriately ridiculous.
years.xp:
Osborne was born in Morton, Washington and moved to Montesano at age 12, according to Wikipedia. The band's early setlists leaned on Hendrix and Cream, and the punk originals came after.

Wikipedia and a Consequence oral history both date the start to 1983, with Osborne on guitar and vocals, Lukin on bass and Dillard on drums.

years.h: [[Dale Crover|9b93a71b-1484-4bea-b096-f660c1161f8a]] replaces Mike Dillard on drums
years.p: Crover, recruited from an Iron Maiden cover band, becomes the second half of a Buzz-and-Dale partnership that runs to this day. Rehearsals move to Aberdeen.

q: When I saw them play, it just blew me away.
years.src: Wikipedia: Buzz Osborne · Wikipedia: Dale Crover
years.h: A young [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] watches the Melvins and turns punk
years.p: Cobain, an Aberdeen kid, attends Melvins rehearsals and shows. That winter he starts Fecal Matter with Dale Crover on bass and Greg Hokanson on drums.
years.xp:
Fecal Matter formed in late 1985 with Cobain, Crover on bass and Hokanson, and recorded the Illiteracy Will Prevail demo around Easter 1986, per Wikipedia. It is the first time Cobain and Crover made music together.

Cobain later described seeing the Melvins for the first time as the moment he became a punk.

years.h: Six Songs on C/Z Records
years.p: First release: a live-in-the-studio session recorded February 8, 1986 at Ironwood Studio in Seattle, out on a 7-inch.
years.xp: The recording was later expanded into the longer reissues known as 10 Songs and 26 Songs, per Wikipedia and Trouser Press.

years.h: Gluey Porch Treatments: the first album
years.p: Recorded in October 1986 at Studio D in Sausalito, California and put out on Alchemy Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Matt Lukin · Wikipedia: Lori Black
years.h: [[Matt Lukin|299e8c0a-63ad-4d49-b492-d3740364da84]] leaves and forms [[Mudhoney|e675295a-1efe-4247-aa3b-53b78d0cdffc]]; [[Lori Black|5a931325-c1f2-4772-840e-3141b9465793]] takes the bass
years.p: Lukin co-founds Mudhoney with Mark Arm, Steve Turner and Dan Peters. Lori Black, a daughter of Shirley Temple, joins as bassist under the name Lorax.
years.xp:
Lukin told it this way, per Wikipedia: Osborne said he was moving to San Francisco and the Melvins would break up. Lukin only later found out that Crover had moved there too and that the band had carried on with Black.

Wikipedia's Lori Black article also says she briefly married Osborne around 1987. Black had earlier played bass in Clown Alley.

eras.title: San Francisco and the Nirvana connection
eras.text: Osborne and Crover move south, the songs get slower and heavier, and the friends they left in Washington get a lot bigger. Crover drums on Nirvana's first demo while the Melvins turn out the records that grunge and doom both trace back to.

years.h: [[Dale Crover|9b93a71b-1484-4bea-b096-f660c1161f8a]] drums on [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]'s first demo, billed as 'Kurt Kovain'
years.p: On January 23, 1988, Crover plays on Nirvana's ten-song demo at Reciprocal Recording in Seattle, and drums with them live in Tacoma the same day. He is credited under a misheard name.
years.xp:
Crover ended up on three tracks of Bleach: 'Floyd the Barber', 'Paper Cuts' and 'Downer', plus material later released on Incesticide and With the Lights Out, per Wikipedia.

He briefly rejoined Nirvana on an August 1990 West Coast tour with Sonic Youth, and drummed on an April 1991 demo with Cobain on guitar and Dave Grohl on bass.

years.h: [[Buzz Osborne|9a911b22-f972-44ee-b2d3-d41297fe96e9]] introduces Dave Grohl to Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic
years.p: After Grohl's Washington, DC band Scream breaks up, Osborne is the one who puts him in touch with Cobain and [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]], according to Wikipedia. Nirvana's drummer problem is solved a couple of years later.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: Osborne and Crover move to San Francisco
years.p: Osborne quits his job and the two relocate, recruiting Lori Black. Osborne says he lived off music from then on, before any Atlantic deal.

years.h: Ozma: produced by [[Mark Deutrom|85cf9aef-aa91-4d8a-9340-04b86ed174d6]]
years.p: First record on Boner Records and the first with Black on bass, credited as Lorax. Deutrom, who produces, joins as bassist a few years later.

years.h: Bullhead: slow, heavy and huge
years.p: The second Boner album stretches the songs and drops the tempo. It is the record that sets the Melvins' drone-sludge template. A Japanese band later took its name from the song 'Boris'.
years.xp: Boris named themselves after the Bullhead song, per Wikipedia. The same year Boner also issued the Eggnog EP, built around a 20-minute experimental piece.

eras.title: Solo EPs, Kurt as producer, and Atlantic
eras.text: The Melvins spoof Kiss, lose a song title to a cleaning-product maker, and sign with Atlantic at Nirvana's suggestion. The big-label chapter starts with Cobain in the control room and ends with one very odd record under a backwards name.

years.h: Three solo EPs, Kiss-style: Buzz, Dale and [[Joe Preston|c0d6e5e6-4919-47c8-a966-b9bbfbaaec72]]
years.p: Boner issues three individual EPs titled King Buzzo, Dale Crover and Joe Preston, a nod to Kiss's four solo albums of 1978. Preston has replaced Black on bass.
years.xp: Preston is on the 1992 Salad of a Thousand Delights and the album released under the name Melvins, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Lysol becomes Melvins after a trademark complaint
years.p: The album was announced as Lysol, but the cleaning-product maker objected. It came out as the self-titled Melvins on Boner and Tupelo, with Joe Preston on bass.

years.cap: The Atlantic debut, recorded in about two weeks in San Francisco and Seattle.
years.src: Wikipedia: Houdini · Life of the Record
years.h: Houdini: the Atlantic Records debut
years.p: Atlantic president Danny Goldberg signs the Melvins at Kurt Cobain's suggestion. The contract gives the band creative control, and the album is cut in roughly two weeks.
years.xp:
The sessions were split across Brilliant Studios and Razor's Edge in San Francisco and the Laundry Room in Seattle. 'Honey Bucket' was released on August 30 and got MTV airplay, per Wikipedia. Osborne told Life of the Record that the album sold over 100,000 copies and that he never expected Atlantic to keep the band beyond one record.

The album also has a cover of Kiss's 'Goin' Blind'.

q: I had no interest in going public with Kurt's problems.
years.src: Louder · Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Houdini
years.h: Cobain is fired from producing Houdini
years.p: Cobain, brought in to co-produce, misses sessions and Osborne asks Atlantic to remove him. Garth Richardson takes over, and Cobain keeps his credit and plays guitar on 'Sky Pup'.
years.xp:
Osborne told Metal Hammer in November 2021 that Cobain was 'a mess, drug-wise' late in the sessions. Atlantic's Goldberg had put it down to scheduling. Osborne also says Cobain played percussion on 'Spread Eagle Beagle'.

Engineer Jonathan Burnside recalled 'bad communication, drugs, major label profiteering, rehab, schedule blowouts'.

years.h: [[Mark Deutrom|85cf9aef-aa91-4d8a-9340-04b86ed174d6]] takes over on bass
years.p: Black, credited on Houdini though Osborne disputes how much she played, is gone by spring. Deutrom, who produced Ozma, stays through 1998.

years.h: Prick: released as ƧИIV⅃ƎM on Amphetamine Reptile Records
years.p: The Melvins still had an Atlantic contract, so the noise record goes to [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s Amphetamine Reptile under a mirror-written band name. Release date is August 5, 1994.
years.xp: Recorded in April 1994. It was first meant to be called Kurt Kobain, but the band changed the title after Cobain's death that month so it wouldn't read as a tribute, per Wikipedia. Osborne has called it a joke record made for the weirdness of it.

years.src: Life of the Record · Wikipedia: Melvins
years.h: Stoner Witch: the second Atlantic album
years.p: Osborne rates it above Houdini, calling that record 'not a high point'. It is the Atlantic record fans point to first.

eras.title: Dropped by Atlantic, home at AmRep
eras.text: Sitar, trombone, a 25-minute silence and a concert in Melbourne. The major-label years end quietly, and the Melvins make their next records for Amphetamine Reptile.

years.h: Stag: sitar, trombone and a Mammoth/Atlantic imprint
years.p: The third and last Atlantic record is the strangest, with sitar and trombone in the mix. It reached number 33 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Melvins · Life of the Record
years.h: Atlantic drops the Melvins after three albums
years.p: The band had expected to be dropped after one. Osborne says the label never interfered with what they recorded.

years.h: Honky: recorded in six days, ends on 25 minutes of silence
years.p: Recorded February 12 to 17, 1997 and released May 5 on Amphetamine Reptile, with Deutrom on bass. The vinyl version drops the silence.

years.src: Wikipedia: Alive at the Fucker Club
years.h: Alive at the F*cker Club: three nights in Melbourne
years.p: A 21-minute live album cut on August 23, 1997 at the Corner Hotel in Richmond, Melbourne, while the Melvins opened for Cosmic Psychos. AmRep released it in 1998.

years.h: [[Kevin Rutmanis|140e4f42-ff95-470b-af7b-bd4be6e96db7]] of The Cows joins on bass
years.p: Deutrom exits and Rutmanis takes the job for the next seven years. Osborne also joins [[Fantômas|057aa66c-cf6e-499d-bda8-5adc47ad4197]] with [[Mike Patton|6e891631-d99c-4768-8bc2-5e5feb42881c]] this year.

eras.title: Patton's label, Biafra and lunch meat
eras.text: Mike Patton's new Ipecac Recordings becomes the Melvins' home and starts a long reissue project. The band spreads out: a trilogy, two collaborations with Jello Biafra, a drone piece with Lustmord and a bass player who vanishes.

years.h: The Melvins sign with Ipecac Recordings
years.p: Mike Patton's label starts remastering and reissuing the back catalog, and puts out the Maggot, Bootlicker and Crybaby records over 1999 and 2000, some with guest vocalists.

years.h: Tool 'sux', in lunch meat
years.p: On an Australian tour the Melvins photograph the words 'Melvins say... Tool Sux!' spelled out in deli meat, and the picture ends up on Tool's own website, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Pigs of the Roman Empire with [[Lustmord|15f2bb82-bce4-44c9-863a-995ae9bde0b4]]
years.p: A slow, heavy collaboration with ambient artist Lustmord on Ipecac.

years.h: Rutmanis is out after an October 2004 tour is cancelled
years.p: A planned European tour is cancelled amid unexplained complications with Rutmanis. He comes back briefly in early 2005 and officially leaves in June.

eras.title: Two drummers, one bunker
eras.text: The two men of Big Business join and the Melvins become a quartet with a pair of fused drum kits. Then a Melvins Lite line-up gets in a van and plays every state in 51 nights.

years.cap: The two-drummer Melvins, with Jared Warren and Coady Willis of [[Big Business]].
years.h: [[Big Business|97bb32a9-a490-403f-8eda-cd33d9466059]] join: two drummers, one wall of sound
years.p: [[Jared Warren|0bc59e8e-4911-4f0f-b851-3a638af30235]] and [[Coady Willis|3e4cad92-f9bf-4a70-8d9e-188aec7d87f2]] become Melvins after the band's Los Angeles move, appearing first on (A) Senile Animal. Crover and Willis fuse two drum sets into a mirror image.
years.xp:
Crover explained the setup this way: Willis is left-handed, so the two play a mirror-image arrangement, with their kits pushed together.

Big Business, the bass-and-drums duo Warren and Willis founded in Seattle in 2004, kept going alongside.

years.h: Melvins play Jello Biafra's 50th birthday shows
years.p: Osborne, Mike Dillard on drums and Crover on bass play two San Francisco shows at the Great American Music Hall, performing only The Mangled Demos.

years.cap: Melvins Lite on the road in 2012.
years.h: All 50 states plus D.C. in 51 nights
years.p: Melvins Lite (Osborne, Crover and [[Trevor Dunn|0dee6bef-335d-4f29-92b2-4d84b0e48552]]) play Anchorage on September 5 and end in Honolulu on October 25, setting a record for consecutive states, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: The tour began the same week as Freak Puke, the Lite record. A tour film, Across the USA in 51 Days: The Movie!, followed.

eras.title: Back to 1983, then bass roulette
eras.text: For the thirtieth anniversary the original drummer returns, Crover moves to bass, and the band starts rotating bassists and collaborators. Steven McDonald of Redd Kross settles in, Coady Willis returns and the Melvins keep releasing at a pace few peers match.

years.h: Tres Cabrones: Mike Dillard is back
years.p: For the 30th anniversary, the Melvins reunite founding drummer [[Mike Dillard|a3750a7b-cf02-4e48-b16c-0b61ca820bfa]] with Osborne and Crover, who plays bass. Ipecac releases the album in November.
years.xp: The album is billed as the closest thing to the original Melvins, per the Consequence oral history. The 1983 line-up recorded again on Working with God (2021) and Thunderball (2025).

years.h: Hold It In with Butthole Surfers' Paul Leary and Jeff Pinkus
years.p: Osborne and Crover team with Paul Leary and Jeff Pinkus of the Butthole Surfers.

years.h: Steven McDonald of [[Redd Kross|d3a4e499-19cf-4676-8aff-4a326b47cdb2]] takes over on bass
years.p: The Big Business pair leave, and Redd Kross's McDonald joins as the Melvins' bassist. He is still there.

years.h: Basses Loaded: a different bassist on almost every track
years.p: McDonald, [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]] of Nirvana, Trevor Dunn, Jared Warren and Jeff Pinkus all take turns.

years.h: Spinal surgery sidelines Crover; Coady Willis returns
years.p: Crover sits out the 2023 tour after spinal surgery and Willis steps back in as second drummer. In 2025 the Melvins co-headline with Napalm Death and release Savage Imperial Death March on February 16.

sources.title: Consequence: Three Bastards, 30 Years, an Oral History of the Melvins
Life of the Record: The Making of Houdini
